question: Which of the following techniques can be used to separate the impurities in Milk?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Column chromatography**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Column Chromatography**

 
 
• The **separation and purification of substances from a solution to obtain the simpler substances from the complex elements is called column chromatography**.
 
• The process of separation employs **five different types of column chromatography**.
 
• The** two phases** of the procedure are the **mobile phase and the stationary phase**. 
 
• In this **solid-liquid method**, the **stationary phase is a solid** and the **mobile phase is a liquid or gas**.
 
• Applications of **Column Chromatography**
 
 
• **separation of** a complex mixture.
 
• **purification** or the process of** removing impurities**.
 
• isolation of the **active elements**.
 
• **removing metabolites **from bodily fluids.
 
• **estimation **of pharmaceutical compounds or crude extracts.
 
• Column Chromatography can also be used to **separate the impurities in Milk**.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microscopy**

 
 
• The** method of viewing things that are invisible to the naked eye is called microscopy**.
 
• ​The **range** can be any value between** mm and nm**.
 
• **Optical microscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and electron microscopy **are the three main microscopic techniques that are used.
 
 
 
• **Microtomy**
 
 
• **Microtomy **is a technique that can be used instead of electropolishing and ion milling **to prepare thin sections for materials like bones, minerals, and teeth**.
 
• The **section thickness of a microtome** can be adjusted to be between** 50 nm and 100 m, thin enough to divide a human hair across its breadth**.
 
 
 
• **Autoclave**
 
 
• An **autoclave is a device used to perform industrial and scientific procedures **that demand for **higher pressure and/or temperature** than ambient conditions.
 
• To **eliminate dangerous germs, viruses, fungus, and spores on objects inside a pressure vessel, steam is used under pressure in this machine**.
